findings.function: name(), symbol(), convertTo(uint256,string,uint256), upgradeToV2(), initialize(...) (both overloads)
findings.decompiled: mem[ceil32(return_data.size) + 128] = mem[mem[128] + 128] / while idx < _3: mem[idx + ceil32(return_data.size) + 160] = mem[_1 + idx + 160] ... / while idx < _9: mem[_7 + idx + 64] = mem[...] / return 32, mem[_7 + 32 len floor32(_9) + 64]
findings.issue: The string returned by the processor is decoded and re-encoded through two 32-byte copy loops plus the partial-word masking of the 0.6 code generator (P7), so name() is ~40 lines for 'return processor.name()' and the DOMAIN_SEPARATOR hashes a memory copy instead of the return data.
findings.rule: Recognise the word-copy loop 'while idx < n: mem[d + idx] = mem[s + idx]; idx += 32' followed by the tail masking as one copy line, then forward reads of the copy to its source (here ext_call.return_data[...]).

notes: solc 0.6.2 build. All 74 ABI functions compared; the two initialize overloads (196 and 210 lines) by structure (initializer flag, the processor register call - P2 -, trustedIntermediaries storage copy and tail clearing, TrustedIntermediariesChanged event, DOMAIN_SEPARATOR), the rest in full. No semantic error found; bulkTransfer/bulkTransferFrom match the source including the Transfer events from the processor's returned (updatedTo, updatedAmount) and the AL01 allowance check. Loops: the three source for-loops (bulkTransfer, bulkTransferFrom's two loops) are readable whiles. The other 20 whiles are implicit: trustedIntermediaries' rotated storage-to-memory copy (P3), the address[] decoding and the masked tail clearing 'address(stor[idx]) = 0' of the storage array assignment, and 14 string/bytes copies (P7).
summary: Faithful and mostly readable; the only recurring cost is the 0.6 string decoding/encoding copy loops (P7) around the processor's string returns and three raw-memory calls.
